applicationClassification.whyOcaml: The compiler has already selected a checked Haxe runtime capability. These modules implement its OCaml carrier or host primitive and are copied through the locked, hashed runtime manifest. Private allocation stamps preserve native ObjectMap lookup across mutation and moving GC. Haxe selects each allocation and class descriptor; OCaml supplies atomic stamps and checked native representation access without interpreting compiler facts.
applicationClassification.readinessRule: A manifest entry proves source ownership and integrity, not full Haxe parity. Missing, stale, unknown, profile-illegal, or semantically unexplained runtime requirements remain fail-closed work under haxe_ocaml-0uwin.

toolingClassifications.whyOcaml: OCaml Dynlink loads the selected native artifact; Haxe validates the manifest, ABI snapshot, provider identity, and compiler-facing meaning.
The OCaml callback registry captures native plugin registrations. Haxe decodes and validates the versioned snapshot before it affects backend selection.
The module owns loopback socket I/O and calls the Haxe request handler. It does not decode compiler arguments, select display behavior, compile, cache, or synthesize semantic responses.
OCaml Dynlink opens the selected macro module and captures registrations. Haxe owns ABI validation, plugin identity, expression selection, request lifetime, and compiler effects.

The OCaml callback registry retains the native closure a plugin registers for each macro declaration, emits a versioned registration snapshot, and passes one opaque payload string to the selected closure. Haxe validates that snapshot, encodes and decodes every payload (MacroSyntaxWire), and owns all compiler-visible macro behavior and cleanup.
